zh.principle: **标准**：联邦信息与组织的信息安全持续监视（SP 800-137）（Information Security Continuous Monitoring (ISCM) for Federal Information Systems and Organizations (SP 800-137)）。主题定义在文首的执行摘要：「Information security continuous monitoring (ISCM) is defined as maintaining ongoing awareness of information security, vulnerabilities, and threats to support organizational risk management decisions.」§1.3 给出本文件的动作：「The purpose of this guideline is to assist organizations in the development of an ISCM strategy and the implementation of an ISCM program that provides awareness of threats and vulnerabilities, visibility into organizational assets, and the effectiveness of deployed security controls.」同段说明其支撑关系：「The ISCM strategy and program support ongoing assurance that planned and implemented security controls are aligned with organizational risk tolerance, as well as the ability to provide the information needed to respond to risk in a timely manner.」扉页标题行把对象限定在联邦一侧：「Information Security Continuous Monitoring (ISCM) for Federal Information Systems and Organizations」。产出是 strategy 与 program 两级：监视什么、多久一次、由谁判断，均归入这两级；控制本身的实现不在本文件内。
zh.why: 理由先给法定下限再给运行理由。§1.1 交代 2002 年法的要求：「The Federal Information Security Management Act (FISMA) of 2002 further emphasized the importance of continuously monitoring information system security by requiring agencies to conduct assessments of security controls at a frequency appropriate to risk, but no less than annually.」再记当年OMB备忘的口径：「The memorandum provides instructions for annual FISMA reporting and emphasizes monitoring the security state of information systems on an ongoing basis with a frequency sufficient to make ongoing, risk-based decisions.」执行摘要给出资源约束下的必要性：「Timely, relevant, and accurate information is vital, particularly when resources are limited and agencies must prioritize their efforts.」以及前提句：「the ability to manage this technology and to assure confidentiality, integrity, and availability of information is now also mission-critical.」四句连读是本文的立场：年度评估是下限而非足够频率，点状评估之间发生的变更与威胁需要以风险相称的持续可见性来覆盖。
zh.used: 谁做什么由 §2.4 的角色条目与第三层的判定句承担，措辞是陈述句而非 shall。§2.4 写首席信息官：「The CIO ensures that an effective ISCM program is established and implemented for the organization」，写授权官：「reviews security status reports and critical security documents and determines if the risk to the organization from operation of the information system remains acceptable.」§3.1 把频率判定落到系统所有者：「System owners determine assessment frequencies of security controls based on drivers from all three tiers.」并把证据交付写成组织政策决定的下限：「Assessment evidence obtained from ISCM is, at a minimum, provided to AOs as often as required by organizational policy.」同一节把风险档次的判定交给风险执行职能：「The risk executive (function) determines the overall organizational risk tolerance and risk mitigation strategy at the organization tier.」§3.2.2 的判据句在此份文本里报为 §3.1.4：「Organizations take the following criteria into consideration when establishing monitoring frequencies for metrics or assessment frequencies for security controls:」其条目之一即控制易变性：「Volatile security controls are assessed more frequently, whether the objective is establishing security control effectiveness or supporting calculation of a metric.」力度因此是本文件的描述性职责加组织政策：年度下限来自 FISMA，不是本文件的规定。
zh.broken: 四处限度层级不同。§3.1 自陈非规定性：「The guidelines below, though not prescriptive, helps to ensure an organization-wide approach to ISCM that best promotes standardized methodologies and consistent practices」。第一章开篇承认自动化的边界：该句印在 CHAPTER ONE 与 INTRODUCTION 两个标题之后、1.1 BACKGROUND 之前的正文段内（留存件在这一页仍印着 PAGE 1 的页面板）：「While this document encourages the use of automation, it is recognized that many aspects of ISCM programs are not easily automated.」执行摘要里另印有 must 级的范围句：「It is important to recognize that with any comprehensive information security program, all implemented security controls, including management and operational controls, must be regularly assessed for effectiveness, even if the monitoring of such controls cannot be automated or is not easily automated.」§2.2 说明频率不是可复制的常量：「Monitoring frequencies (e.g., annually, quarterly, monthly, daily) are not static, and they are not uniform across all metrics.」Authority 段两处限定：「such standards and guidelines shall not apply to national security systems without the express approval of appropriate federal officials exercising policy authority over such systems.」与「This publication may be used by nongovernmental organizations on a voluntary basis and is not subject to copyright in the United States.」即这份指南的限度是层级之别而非有无之别：§3.1 自称非规定性，执行摘要却仍落下 must 级的评估范围，并非一律不作规定；自动化覆盖不到全部流程，频率须按组织自定，国家安全系统的适用另需批准，非政府组织使用纯属自愿。
zh.history: 扉页编号行「NIST Special Publication 800-137」，标题行给出 ISCM 缩写与联邦限定，作者行按序列出八人「Kelley Dempsey Nirali Shah Chawla Arnold Johnson Ronald Johnston Alicia Clay Jones Angela Orebaugh Matthew Scholl Kevin Stine」，日期行在扉页上以大写排印为 SEPTEMBER 2011，其下为部与局的署名列「Patrick D.Gallagher, Under Secretary for Standards and Technology and Director」。Authority 页给出依据与规模：「This publication has been developed by NIST to further its statutory responsibilities under the Federal Information Security Management Act (FISMA), Public Law (P.L.) 107-347.」与分行印出的「NIST Special Publication 800-137, 80 pages」，其下一行单独印出括注日期 (September 2011)——本副本里页数与日期是两行，并非连排一行。致谢页把八位作者按单位分开：「The authors, Kelley Dempsey, Arnold Johnson, Matthew Scholl and Kevin Stine of the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), Ronald Johnston of the Department of Defense Chief Information Officer, Defense-wide Information Assurance Program (DOD-CIO, DIAP), Alicia Clay Jones and Angela Orebaugh of Booz Allen Hamilton, and Nirali Shah Chawla of PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP (PwC), wish to thank their colleagues who reviewed drafts of this document and contributed to its technical content.」这份副本无 DOI 行，标题页也无修订号或取代声明；本份文本还把章节标题的行内连字符丢掉（IS CM 与 RES PONS IBILITIES），故未据章节标题断言任何版次事实。

en.principle: **Standard**: Information Security Continuous Monitoring (ISCM) for Federal Information Systems and Organizations (SP 800-137) (联邦信息与组织的信息安全持续监视（SP 800-137）). The subject definition sits in the Executive Summary at the front: "Information security continuous monitoring (ISCM) is defined as maintaining ongoing awareness of information security, vulnerabilities, and threats to support organizational risk management decisions." Section 1.3 gives the action of the document: "The purpose of this guideline is to assist organizations in the development of an ISCM strategy and the implementation of an ISCM program that provides awareness of threats and vulnerabilities, visibility into organizational assets, and the effectiveness of deployed security controls." The same paragraph states what it supports: "The ISCM strategy and program support ongoing assurance that planned and implemented security controls are aligned with organizational risk tolerance, as well as the ability to provide the information needed to respond to risk in a timely manner." The title block confines the object to the federal side: "Information Security Continuous Monitoring (ISCM) for Federal Information Systems and Organizations". The output is two-level, strategy and program: what is monitored, how often, and who judges it belong to those two levels, while implementing the controls is not.
en.why: The argument gives the statutory floor first and then the operational reason. Section 1.1 records what the 2002 statute required: "The Federal Information Security Management Act (FISMA) of 2002 further emphasized the importance of continuously monitoring information system security by requiring agencies to conduct assessments of security controls at a frequency appropriate to risk, but no less than annually." It then records the reporting posture of the year: "The memorandum provides instructions for annual FISMA reporting and emphasizes monitoring the security state of information systems on an ongoing basis with a frequency sufficient to make ongoing, risk-based decisions." The Executive Summary supplies the resource constraint, "Timely, relevant, and accurate information is vital, particularly when resources are limited and agencies must prioritize their efforts." and the premise "the ability to manage this technology and to assure confidentiality, integrity, and availability of information is now also mission-critical." Read together, annual assessment is a floor rather than a sufficient frequency, and the changes and threats that arrive between point-in-time assessments need continuous visibility matched to risk.
en.used: Who acts is carried by the role entries of §2.4 and the decision sentences at the system tier, stated as plain present tense rather than shall. Section 2.4 says of the chief information officer "The CIO ensures that an effective ISCM program is established and implemented for the organization" and of the authorizing official "reviews security status reports and critical security documents and determines if the risk to the organization from operation of the information system remains acceptable." Section 3.1 puts frequency decisions on the system owner: "System owners determine assessment frequencies of security controls based on drivers from all three tiers." and sets evidence delivery at a policy-determined floor: "Assessment evidence obtained from ISCM is, at a minimum, provided to AOs as often as required by organizational policy." The same section assigns the risk bar to the risk executive (function): "The risk executive (function) determines the overall organizational risk tolerance and risk mitigation strategy at the organization tier." The criteria sentence from §3.2.2 reports as §3.1.4 in this text: "Organizations take the following criteria into consideration when establishing monitoring frequencies for metrics or assessment frequencies for security controls:" one item of which is control volatility: "Volatile security controls are assessed more frequently, whether the objective is establishing security control effectiveness or supporting calculation of a metric." The obligation level is therefore this document describing duties plus organizational policy: the annual floor comes from FISMA, not from here.
en.broken: The four limits work at different levels. Section 3.1 states its own non-prescriptiveness: "The guidelines below, though not prescriptive, helps to ensure an organization-wide approach to ISCM that best promotes standardized methodologies and consistent practices". The boundary of automation is conceded in the opening body of Chapter One, where the sentence prints after the CHAPTER ONE and INTRODUCTION headings and before 1.1 BACKGROUND on a page this copy still labels PAGE 1: "While this document encourages the use of automation, it is recognized that many aspects of ISCM programs are not easily automated." The Executive Summary separately prints must-level scope: "It is important to recognize that with any comprehensive information security program, all implemented security controls, including management and operational controls, must be regularly assessed for effectiveness, even if the monitoring of such controls cannot be automated or is not easily automated." Section 2.2 denies that frequencies are transferable constants: "Monitoring frequencies (e.g., annually, quarterly, monthly, daily) are not static, and they are not uniform across all metrics." The Authority block adds two bounds: "such standards and guidelines shall not apply to national security systems without the express approval of appropriate federal officials exercising policy authority over such systems." and "This publication may be used by nongovernmental organizations on a voluntary basis and is not subject to copyright in the United States." So the limits differ by level rather than by existence: Section 3.1 calls itself non-prescriptive while the Executive Summary still states a must-level assessment scope, so the guideline is not silent about obligations; automation does not reach every process, frequencies are set per organisation, national security systems need express approval, and non-governmental use is purely voluntary.
en.history: The title block carries "NIST Special Publication 800-137", a part title that spells out ISCM and confines it to federal systems, and the author line naming eight people in order, "Kelley Dempsey Nirali Shah Chawla Arnold Johnson Ronald Johnston Alicia Clay Jones Angela Orebaugh Matthew Scholl Kevin Stine", with the date line set in capitals on the title block and the signing officials below it, of whom "Patrick D. Gallagher, Under Secretary for Standards and Technology and Director". The Authority page gives the basis, "This publication has been developed by NIST to further its statutory responsibilities under the Federal Information Security Management Act (FISMA), Public Law (P.L.) 107-347.", then puts the extent and the date on two separate printed lines: "NIST Special Publication 800-137, 80 pages" and, on the next line, the date in parentheses (September 2011). The page count and the date are not run together in this copy. The acknowledgements split the eight authors by employer: "The authors, Kelley Dempsey, Arnold Johnson, Matthew Scholl and Kevin Stine of the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), Ronald Johnston of the Department of Defense Chief Information Officer, Defense-wide Information Assurance Program (DOD-CIO, DIAP), Alicia Clay Jones and Angela Orebaugh of Booz Allen Hamilton, and Nirali Shah Chawla of PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP (PwC), wish to thank their colleagues who reviewed drafts of this document and contributed to its technical content." This copy has no DOI line and no revision or supersession statement; the extraction also drops interior hyphens from headings (IS CM, RES PONS IBILITIES), so no edition fact is taken from a heading.

zh: information security continuous monitoring (ISCM)：为维护信息安全、脆弱性与威胁的持续知晓以支撑风险管理决定的过程。
ISCM strategy：按组织层级界定监视内容、频率与判据的策略，风险容忍度是其依据。
ISCM program：按既定度量收集信息的计划安排，信息部分来自已实现的控制。
monitoring frequency：某项度量的观测频次，随风险、变更与威胁信息调整。
assessment frequency：某项控制 effectiveness 的评估频次，可由系统所有者按三层驱动确定。
risk tolerance：主体为达成期望结果愿意承担的风险水平（本文件沿用 NISTIR 7298 定义）。
en: Information security continuous monitoring (ISCM): maintaining ongoing awareness of information security, vulnerabilities and threats to support risk management decisions.
ISCM strategy: the tier-level definition of what is monitored, how often and on what criteria, grounded in organizational risk tolerance.
ISCM program: the arrangement that collects information according to preestablished metrics, using data partly available from implemented controls.
Monitoring frequency: how often a metric is observed, adjusted for risk, change and threat information.
Assessment frequency: how often control effectiveness is assessed, which system owners set from drivers at all three tiers.
Risk tolerance: the level of risk an entity is willing to assume to achieve a potential desired result, following the NISTIR 7298 definition.
